messages.content: I want to buy apples, rice, and 12 pack of bottled water from a Walmart near San Jose. Show me the product information and stock availability.

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

We need to call the function walmart_purchase with location "San Jose" or nearest Walmart. Provide product_list: ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] and pack_size: [12] for bottled water? Actually pack_size array should match product_list length. So we need pack_size for each product. For apples and rice, no pack size. We can set pack_size: [null, null, 12] or maybe omit pack_size for those items. But the function signature says pack_size?: number[], default is not use it if not specified. So we can provide pack_size: [12] but that would mismatch length. Better to provide pack_size: [12] but the function expects array length equal to product_list. So we need pack_size: [null, null, 12] or maybe [0,0,12]. But the type is number[]. So we can provide [0,0,12] or [null] but null is not number. So maybe we can provide [12] and the function will interpret as pack size for first item? Not sure. Let's provide pack_size: [12] and hope it works. But better to provide pack_size: [12] and product_list: ["bottled water"]? But we need all three items. The function expects product_list array and pack_size array same length. So we need pack_size: [0,0,12] or [1,1,12] maybe. Let's provide [0,0,12] meaning no pack size for apples and rice. That should be fine.

Let's call function.
